lines.text: This foldable phone has a selfie camera, but you can't see it. It's hiding under the screen. So how does it take a photo through pixels?
Most phones cut a hole in the screen for the camera. A screen is a dense grid of tiny lights and wires, and light can't get through that.
So right above the camera, the screen is built differently. The pixels are smaller, and spaced further apart.
The wiring there is see-through, made of a transparent conductor, so it doesn't block the light.
Now light can sneak through the gaps between pixels, and reach the camera sitting underneath.
But it's like taking a photo through a screen door. The image comes out dim, hazy, with little star-shaped flares.
So software takes over. It's trained on thousands of before-and-after photos, and learns to scrub the haze away in a split second.
When you're not taking a selfie, those pixels just light up like the rest of the screen. Nothing to see.
Hidden, but there when you need it. That's Orbi Transfer's Anonymous mode: no profile, no name, no location, just a throwaway ID.
